panel_name: Environmental Control and Cognitive Offloading Calibration Panel
purpose: Calibrate mechanisms related to personal environmental control and cognitive offloading. Environmental mastery (control over thermostat, blinds, furniture) and externalization of working memory to the environment are critical for workplace satisfaction and cognitive performance.

target_templates.name: Environmental Mastery / Control
target_templates.mechanism: Personal CONTROL over environment (thermostat, blinds, furniture position, etc.) as independent predictor of satisfaction and stress reduction. Distinct from social territory (SOC templates).
target_templates.architectural_relevance: Offices, healthcare, residential. Sense of control reduces stress even when control is not exercised. Perceived controllability matters as much as actual control.

target_templates.name: Cognitive Offloading
target_templates.mechanism: Externalization of working memory to environment (notes, displays, spatial arrangements). Environment as extended mind.
target_templates.architectural_relevance: Workplaces, educational, creative spaces. Designing environments that support cognitive offloading reduces WM load and improves performance.

constructs_to_calibrate.name: perceived_control_baseline
constructs_to_calibrate.description: Baseline perceived control in typical office environment
constructs_to_calibrate.current_status: validated scales exist, needs architectural operationalization

constructs_to_calibrate.name: control_stress_effect
constructs_to_calibrate.description: Stress reduction from perceived environmental control

constructs_to_calibrate.name: control_elements_weight
constructs_to_calibrate.description: Relative importance of different controllable features
constructs_to_calibrate.current_status: thermal > lighting > acoustic in most studies

constructs_to_calibrate.name: wm_offloading_benefit
constructs_to_calibrate.description: Working memory load reduction from environmental supports
constructs_to_calibrate.current_status: established in cognitive science, not applied to architecture

constructs_to_calibrate.name: display_surface_threshold
constructs_to_calibrate.description: Minimum writable/display surface for effective offloading
constructs_to_calibrate.current_status: preliminary estimates in CREA4, needs validation

key_papers.contribution: Building Use Studies database. Personal control strongly predicts satisfaction.
Personal environmental control and sick building syndrome.
Job demands-control model. Control buffers stress effects.
Cognitive offloading review. Humans strategically offload to environment.
Extended mind hypothesis. Cognition extends into environment.

design_features: Personal thermal control (operable windows, individual thermostats)
population_sensitivity: Older workers value thermal control more
Creative workers need more offloading surfaces
Individual differences in control preference (high vs. low)

pre_reading: Understand extended cognition and cognitive offloading
calibration_protocol: 1. Define control elements and their relative weights
2. Map perceived control to stress and satisfaction outcomes
3. Parameterize cognitive offloading surfaces and features
5. Define interaction with SOC templates (territorial vs. control)
6. Create WIS conversion from control parameters
output_deliverables: Updated T15 template JSON with calibrated parameters
New cognitive_offloading template (T28) with calibrated parameters
Offloading surface recommendations by task type
